ashtakavarga.caption:
ur chart contains exactly 337 points and they are not evenly spread 📊

ashtakavarga is the part of jyotish that behaves like arithmetic. eight reference points, the seven grahas plus ur lagna, each vote on every sign by fixed rules. no interpretation anywhere in the counting.

add the seven grahas up and every sign scores from 0 to 56. the twelve always total 337, so an average sign gets about 28. above 30 is a dense house. under 25 is a thin one.

which means a chart cannot be good everywhere. if one sign scores well another is scoring badly, by arithmetic, and astrology is not often that honest about trade offs.

it is also the reason two people in sade sati at the same time in the same signs can have completely different readings: same sky, different bindu count.

three-saturns.caption:
there are three different saturn periods and the internet calls all of them sade sati ⚖️

one. sade sati: saturn crossing the 12th, 1st and 2nd from ur moon sign. seven and a half years, once per saturn cycle, and it can begin at any age depending on ur chart.

two. shani dhaiya: saturn in the 4th or the 8th from ur moon, about thirty months each. kantaka shani and ashtama shani. twice per cycle.

three. the saturn return: saturn back at the exact degree it held at ur birth. that one is western, it lands at about 29 for everybody, and it is measured against natal saturn rather than ur moon. vedic astrology has no saturn return doctrine because the dasha system already covers life stages.

the twist: a saturn return happens on the same date in both zodiacs, because a return to a physical position cancels the 24 degree offset. sade sati does not, because it counts whole signs.
